world.era: 17th century (composed 1658–1667) intercut with the poem's own mythic cosmos and with present-day analogies the hosts draw
world.setting: Two worlds run in parallel all episode. One is Milton's: a blind, politically defeated poet dictating an epic in a dark London room after the Restoration. The other is the poem's: heaven, the burning lake, Pandemonium, the abyss, Mount Niphates, Eden. The hosts constantly cut to a third, modern register — a fired CEO in a dumpster, a rigged corporate town hall, a 3 a.m. ceiling, a curated social feed — so modern imagery is DELIBERATE here, not an anachronism.
world.register: Two sharp readers arguing about a poem they love; analytic, funny, unafraid of the theology.

satan.name: Satan
satan.role: The poem's great self-persuader: a defeated rebel who rebrands his own catastrophe and cannot stop performing.
satan.look: A tall, powerfully built fallen angel in his forties, dark hair swept back, handsome and scorched, wearing charred dark armor over a deep crimson cloak with singed ragged wings.

milton.name: John Milton
milton.role: The blind poet dictating the epic in the dark — the defeated republican who refuses to give himself the good lines.
milton.look: A blind Englishman in his fifties, shoulder-length grey hair, pale clouded eyes, plain dark 17th-century doublet with a white falling band collar, seated upright in a wooden chair.

eve.name: Eve
eve.role: Wins her argument with Milton's own logic, then finishes the serpent's case herself.
eve.look: A young woman with long loose auburn hair, barefoot in a simple pale draped shift, standing among garden leaves.

adam.name: Adam
adam.role: Not deceived — he does the math, and eats anyway.
adam.look: A young man with dark curling hair and a beard, barefoot in a simple draped tunic, holding a garland of woven flowers.

abdiel.name: Abdiel
abdiel.role: The one angel who stands alone against millions and calls the lie — Milton's self-portrait.
abdiel.look: A solitary angel in a plain white robe with a simple rope belt, short fair hair, no armor, standing straight-backed and unarmed.

beelzebub.name: Beelzebub
beelzebub.role: Satan's chief of staff, who tables the plan Satan wrote before the meeting started.
beelzebub.look: A grave, majestic fallen angel with close-cropped grey hair and heavy shoulders, in a dark formal mantle over dulled armor.

michael.name: Michael
michael.role: Escorts the couple out and hands them the corrected version of Satan's own idea.
michael.look: An archangel in burnished pale armor with a plain sword at his side, calm, close-cropped dark hair, broad white wings folded.

bentley.name: Richard Bentley
bentley.role: The 1732 scholar who invented a phantom editor rather than admit the blind poet outclassed him — the episode's running metaphor for the ego.
bentley.look: A heavy-set 18th-century scholar in a powdered wig and dark academic gown, quill in hand, bent over a marked-up folio.

burningLake.look: A lake of fire under a black sky — 'darkness visible': orange-red light with no brightness in it, smoke, a scorched shore of cooling slag.

pandemonium.look: The rebel capital: a vast gold-columned council hall mined out of the soil of hell, a raised podium, ranked seats in shadow — an imitation of heaven built by the people who lost it.

mountNiphates.look: A bare rock summit at dawn, the sun full in frame, the green curve of the new world far below — the one place in the poem where nobody is watching.

eden.look: A dense, orderly garden at morning: heavy fruiting branches, flowers propped on stakes, paths of trimmed green, one tree standing apart.

heaven.look: Open luminous cloud-country, ranked light, no horizon line — the north of heaven where the rebellion is recruited.

miltonsRoom.look: A dark London room before dawn: a single candle, a plain wooden chair, a writing table with blank paper waiting for a secretary who has not arrived yet, shutters closed.

bentleysStudy.look: An 18th-century scholar's study walled with folios, one huge edition of Paradise Lost open under a lamp, margins savaged with ink corrections.

boardroom.look: A glass-walled corporate meeting room mid-town-hall: rows of chairs, a mic stand for questions, a slide already written before anyone spoke.

modernNight.look: A dark bedroom at 3 a.m., ceiling lit by a phone screen face-up on the sheets — the hour with no audience to perform for.

feedStreet.look: A night street where every face is lit from below by a phone: the externalized phantom editor, everyone inside a feed of their own making.

objects.why: The burning lake is the poem's opening image and the episode's running one: the slogan is spoken standing in it.
'High disdain to mask his absolute ruin' — the performance Satan cannot drop, and the phantom editor's whole method.
'Myself am hell' — the moment the mind turns out to be the place. Every private-confession beat is a mirror beat.
The maximum-security prison of the self: he is both inmate and warden.
The manuscript, Bentley's savaged edition, Areopagitica — the poem as a physical text being rewritten by egos.
Dictation, records of light, the erased names, the pre-written plan tabled at the council.
Lucifer's light, the sun at Niphates, the glory he cannot look at without remembering.
The fruit — the one object the whole second half turns on.
The tree of knowledge, and Eden as a place of pruning and growth.
The gates of Eden closing forever; also the slammed door of the teenager analogy.
The flaming sword that drops behind them at the expulsion.
The war in heaven and Moloch's argument for open suicidal war.
Pandemonium, mined out of hell's gold — and the 'digital pandemoniums' of the closing turn.
Kingship runs through everything: 'better to reign', Charles I and II, Louis XIV, 'king of a ruined paradigm'. NO ICON YET — worth drawing.
The hierarchy the poem asserts and keeps undercutting. NO ICON YET — worth drawing.
'Justify the ways of God to men' — the scoreboard the hosts say Milton loses by.
The final image: the world all before them, wandering steps and slow.
The phantom editor itself — the second self that rewrites the record while you sleep.
Hierarchy and the fall from it: heaven's ranks, 'He for God only, she for God in him'.
Chaos: nine days falling through a roaring unformed abyss.

spine.claim: The most quoted line in the poem is a lie, and its speaker is the first person it destroys.
Milton dictated an infinite cosmos from total darkness and total political defeat — and Bentley's phantom editor shows what an ego does instead.
'The mind is its own place' is a PR statement issued minutes after a humiliating defeat, not a philosophy.
Alone on Niphates the performance stops and the line collapses into 'myself am hell'.
Pandemonium turns private self-deception into a political system: a meeting whose outcome was written before it began.
He could repent and refuses — for his reputation among people he does not respect. 'Evil be thou my good' is a grievance hardening into an identity.
To keep the grievance he must deny he was ever created; Abdiel, alone, refuses the lie, and Milton gives himself none of the good lines.
Eve wins the separation argument with Milton's own Areopagitica logic, then finishes the serpent's case herself.
Adam is not deceived — he chooses her over paradise, and the poem calls that a failure dressed as romance.
By his own scoreboard Milton loses; the poem's greatness is that it refuses to look away from its own contradiction.
Michael hands the ruined couple Satan's exact claim, corrected — 'a paradise within thee' — and they walk out into an ordinary first morning.
